transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. To start, can you tell me what brings you in today?

Um, yeah… I guess what brings me in is I feel like I can’t really settle in my own body anymore. Like when I’m supposed to sit quietly and deal with paperwork, or go over household plans with someone, I just feel… restless, like I’m crawling out of my skin a little.

It’s not even dramatic stuff, it’s like forms, bills, figuring out who’s doing what around the house — and then somehow I’m up, or shifting around, or I just can’t stay with it. Sorry, I’m already kind of circling the point. It’s that “I can’t sit and handle normal adult things” feeling that made me think I should talk to someone.
Has this kind of restlessness and difficulty settling down to handle tasks been a lifelong pattern for you, or is it something that started more recently?

No, it’s definitely not new. I mean, I can remember it way back in elementary school. I was that kid with the disaster desk, papers shoved everywhere, permission slips that never made it home or never made it back.

And teachers would write those little notes, like, that I was talking when I wasn’t supposed to, or getting up, or just… not staying seated. I remember one teacher had this whole system with stickers—sorry, that’s not really the point—but yeah, looking back, it feels like it was already there when I was pretty young.
Do you often find yourself losing track of what you're doing, forgetting appointments or belongings, or having trouble focusing on tasks even when you're not feeling anxious or worried?

Yeah, yes. That happens a lot. Like I’ll fully mean to return a call or pay a bill, and then somehow it’s three days later and I’m like, “Oh no, I never did that.”

Or I’ll be going to a meeting or an appointment and realize when I’m already in the car that I forgot the thing I was supposed to bring. And then I start mentally trying to figure out if I can turn around, or if it’s too late, and—sorry, I’m getting off track—but yeah, it’s not always because I’m worried. It’s just like the thing disappears from my brain until it’s suddenly a problem.
Do you often find yourself interrupting others, blurting out answers or comments before someone finishes speaking, or having trouble waiting your turn in conversations or lines?

Yeah… I do. I really try not to, because I care a lot about being respectful, especially with my husband. But I’ll jump in while he’s talking, or I’ll finish what I think someone is about to say.

It’s like the response is already there and it comes out before I’ve made myself wait. And then afterward I’m like, “Why did I do that?” I don’t mean to take over, it just happens fast.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports a lifelong (since elementary school) pattern of both inattentive symptoms (forgetting tasks/appointments, losing track of belongings, difficulty completing paperwork) and hyperactive-impulsive symptoms (restlessness, inability to sit still, interrupting others, blurting responses). Symptoms are present across multiple settings (home, work/task management, social interactions), are not better explained by anxiety alone, and cause functional impairment in daily adult responsibilities. The combination of significant inattentive and hyperactive-impulsive symptoms meeting duration and childhood-onset criteria supports ADHD, Combined Presentation (F90.2), rather than a predominantly inattentive or hyperactive-impulsive subtype.
